title: Mean-Reverting Portfolio Design with Budget Constraint

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper formulates mean-reverting portfolio (MRP) design for statistical arbitrage as an optimization problem that minimizes a mean-reversion criterion (such as predictability, portmanteau, crossing statistics, or penalized crossing statistics) subject to portfolio variance and budget constraints (dollar-neutral or net-budget). The nonconvex optimization problems are solved efficiently either directly via Generalized Eigenvalue Problems (GEVP) and Generalized Trust Region Subproblems (GTRS), or iteratively via a Majorization-Minimization (MM) framework (IRGEVP, IRGTRS, and EIRGEVP). The resulting MRPs are evaluated out-of-sample using a threshold-based mean-reversion trading strategy on log-price spreads.
extraction.data_period: February 1st, 2012 to June 30th, 2014 for market data experiments; synthetic data also used
extraction.universe: S&P 500 Index stock pools and synthetic cointegrated asset systems
key_findings: The proposed mean-reverting portfolio design methods successfully generate consistent positive profits.
Proposed MRP design methods outperform traditional benchmark methods and single underlying spreads in terms of cumulative P&L and Sharpe ratio of returns on investment (ROI).
The reformulation of non-convex MRP design problems into GEVPs and GTRSs allows for efficient computation.
limitations: Asset pool construction is not elaborated in the paper.
extraction.extraction_notes: The paper presents extensive mathematical derivations, algorithmic frameworks (GEVP, GTRS, MM), and visual plots of backtest results (ROIs, Sharpe ratios, cumulative P&Ls) in figures 4, 5, 7, and 8. However, because no explicit numeric performance tables or numerical values for Sharpe ratios/returns are printed in the text or figure labels, the performance_metrics list is left empty in strict accordance with the quantitative metric instructions.
